Consult Summary:
- 42-year-old woman (DOB 20 Apr 1983) with acute-onset shortness of breath for ~1 hour while at rest, new cough since yesterday, and awareness of a rapid heart rate; recent cesarean section 4 weeks ago — clinician concerned for possible pulmonary embolism and advised urgent hospital assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Acute shortness of breath beginning approximately one hour before the consult while sitting and watching TV.
  - New cough started yesterday (patient reports non-productive; no sputum described).
  - Subjective palpitations / increased awareness of heart rate.
  - Chest feels sore on deep inspiration; patient attributes some chest tenderness to recent C-section scar.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Cough began yesterday.
  - Shortness of breath began acutely over the last hour; patient reports this is new and has not occurred previously.
  - Codeine used regularly after C-section but likely stopped about one week ago.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Occurred at rest; no specific exacerbating or relieving factors reported.
  - Patient feels more anxious/stressed because of symptoms.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems (as reported):
  - No hemoptysis reported.
  - No reported pleuritic chest pain (only soreness on deep inspiration attributed to surgical site).
  - No reported leg pain or swelling.
  - No fever or other systemic symptoms reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No prior similar episodes.
  - No other chronic medical problems reported.

Past Medical History:
- Recent obstetric history:
  - Cesarean section 4 weeks ago; postoperative course not otherwise described.
- Other medical history:
  - Patient states she has no other medical problems (none documented).
- Surgical history:
  - Cesarean section (4 weeks prior).
- Complications:
  - None documented.

Medications:
- Codeine — taken fairly regularly after C-section; not taken for approximately 1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other current medications documented.
- Allergies:
  - Ibuprofen — reaction not specified.

Social History:
- Lives with newborn baby (baby present at home during consult).
- Partner at work (not present).
- Occupation / smoking / alcohol / substance use: not recorded.

Family History:
- Mother had clots in her legs (family history of venous thromboembolism).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Clinician-performed pulse check: patient counted 30 beats during the clinician's timed count; clinician described heart rate as "slightly fast" at the time of the consult. (No numeric BPM, blood pressure, respiratory rate, temperature, or oxygen saturation recorded.)
- Examination findings:
  - Not recorded (no formal physical exam documented beyond pulse palpation).

Investigations:
- None performed or available during this consult.
- Clinician advised urgent hospital assessment for further evaluation of possible clot; no specific tests/labs/imaging were ordered in the virtual consult itself.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Acute-onset dyspnea with new cough and subjective tachycardia in a patient 4 weeks postpartum after cesarean section — clinician concerned for possible pulmonary embolism and advised urgent ED evaluation. This impression is consistent with the provided DDx ranking, which places PE as the top concern.
- DDx Integration (brief):
  - 1) Pulmonary embolism — supported by recent C-section (4 weeks postpartum), sudden-onset dyspnea, subjective tachycardia, and family history of VTE; opposing: no hemoptysis, no leg symptoms, no objective vital signs recorded.
  - 2) Acute respiratory infection (pneumonia/bronchitis, viral) — supported by new cough beginning yesterday; opposing: very sudden onset of significant dyspnea and no fever/sputum documented.
  - 3) Peripartum (postpartum) cardiomyopathy — supported by timing in postpartum period and new dyspnea/palpitations; opposing: no preceding progressive symptoms or signs of heart failure documented.
- Issue 1: Suspected pulmonary embolism (primary immediate concern)
  - Assessment:
    - Recent major surgery (C-section 4 weeks ago) and acute dyspnea/tachycardia increase concern for PE.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent hospital/ED assessment recommended for evaluation of possible PE.
    - Options discussed: ambulance vs. self-transport; patient elected to travel to hospital herself with the baby and to go promptly.
    - Advised not to take codeine prior to hospital travel.
    - Safety netting: if symptoms worsen (e.g., severe breathlessness, collapse), call emergency services/ambulance.
    - ED evaluation anticipated (per clinician) may lead to immediate treatment (e.g., anticoagulation) if clot confirmed.
- Issue 2: Acute respiratory infection (differential)
  - Assessment:
    - New cough since yesterday could reflect bronchitis or early pneumonia contributing to dyspnea.
  - Plan:
    - ED assessment will evaluate for respiratory infection as part of the workup.
    - Supportive care as directed by ED clinicians; further decisions (antibiotics, imaging) to be made after clinical assessment.
- Issue 3: Postpartum cardiopulmonary considerations (peripartum cardiomyopathy, anemia)
  - Assessment:
    - Postpartum cardiomyopathy and postpartum anemia are possible contributors to dyspnea in the postpartum period and are included in the differential.
  - Plan:
    - ED assessment to evaluate cardiac function and hematologic status as clinically indicated.
    - Follow-up with primary care / obstetrics postpartum team after ED visit as recommended.
- General plan items:
  - Patient to go to hospital promptly with baby; clinician offered ambulance if needed.
  - Do not take codeine before arrival to hospital.
  - Bring essential items for baby; partner not present but patient able to travel alone.
  - Follow-up arranged as per ED / local care; patient to seek emergency services if condition deteriorates.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No objective vital signs recorded (blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature).
  - No formal physical examination findings documented beyond pulse palpation.
  - No laboratory or imaging results available.
  - Medication dose/route/frequency for codeine not documented.
  - Ibuprofen allergy reaction details not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None identified; DDx prioritization (PE high) is consistent with clinician assessment and advice in the transcript.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/dialogue intelligible with occasional hesitations; essential history clearly documented.
